tg001.tt:
Students studying in Japan wrote compositions on "My days off" and read them in front of the whole class.

(1) Maria's composition
I often go to the park on Sundays. The park is near my house. At the park I read books, take walks, and so on. But last Sunday it rained, so I studied Japanese at home.

(2) Kim's composition
On my days off I cook with my friends. Last week we made curry. It was very delicious. Next Sunday we plan to make a cake.

blanks.e: 〜に あります: to be located at.
でも: but. She usually goes to the park, but that day it rained.
A habit: present tense.
こんどの: next (goes with つもり).

tg002.tt:
International students wrote compositions on "My favorite food".

(1) Tom's composition
I like sushi. I had never eaten it in my country, but after coming to Japan I tried it for the first time. It was very delicious. Now I eat it every week.

(2) Lin's composition
I like ramen. There is a good restaurant near the school. That restaurant is cheap and tasty. I always have lunch at that restaurant.

blanks.e: 〜た ことが ない: to have never done.
とても + affirmative.
やすくて + something positive: おいしいです.
その: the restaurant already mentioned in the text.

tg003.tt:
In Japanese class, students wrote compositions on "My family".

(1) Anna's composition
There are four people in my family: my father, my mother, my older brother and me. My brother is a university student and lives in Tokyo. I want to see him.

(2) John's composition
I have a younger sister. She is 8 years old. My sister is good at singing. She sings at home every day. I like listening to my sister's songs.

blanks.e: 〜に すんで いる: to live in.
ます-stem + たい: あいたい.
わたしの いもうと: my sister.
dictionary form + のが すき.

tg004.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "Things that surprised me in Japan".

(1) Paul's composition
Trains in Japan arrive on time. Trains in my country are often late. So I was surprised.

(2) Mei's composition
Japanese convenience stores have all sorts of things. Not only food and drinks, but also notebooks and pens. They are open until late at night, so they are very convenient. I go to a convenience store every day.

blanks.e: だから: so, that's why (consequence).
Tricky one: 〜だけで なく, not only… but also.
おそくまで あいて いる: open until late.
A habit (まいにち): present tense.

tg005.tt:
International students wrote compositions on "My town".

(1) Han's composition
My town is near the sea. In summer lots of people come and it is very lively. But in winter there are few people and it is quiet.

(2) Sara's composition
There is a mountain in my town. That mountain isn't very high, so even children can climb it. When I was a child, I often climbed it with my father. You can see the town well from the top of the mountain.

blanks.e: A general description: present tense.
その: the mountain just mentioned.
よく: often (affirmative).
Tricky one: みえる, to be visible.

tg006.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "What I did on the weekend".

(1) Lee's composition
On Saturday I went to the department store with a friend. I wanted to buy shoes, but there weren't any good ones. So I didn't buy anything.

(2) Ken's composition
On Sunday I got up early in the morning and went fishing in the river. I caught five fish. I went home and ate the fish with my mother.

blanks.e: 〜たいと おもう: to want to do.
それで: so, therefore.
かえって (and then) + the next action.
その さかな: those fish (already mentioned).

tg007.tt:
In Japanese class, students wrote compositions on "My hobby".

(1) Daniel's composition
My hobby is taking photos. On my days off I take my camera and go to various places. Then I show the photos I took to my friends.

(2) Yun's composition
My hobby is cooking. I make food from my country and also Japanese food. I'm still bad at Japanese cooking, but I practice every week. Someday I want to make delicious tempura.

blanks.e: しゅみは 〜こと です.
そして: and then.
まだ へた (still not good at it) ですが.
ます-stem + たい.

tg008.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "Last year's summer holidays".

(1) Emma's composition
During last year's summer holidays, I went to Hokkaido with friends. Hokkaido was cooler than Tokyo. We ate lots of delicious things every day.

(2) Mike's composition
I didn't go anywhere during the summer holidays, because I was busy with my part-time job. But I saved money from my job, so I plan to go on a trip this winter.

blanks.e: A は B より: more… than.
どこへも + past negative.
He saved money, so he will travel.
dictionary form + つもり.

tg009.tt:
International students living in Japan wrote compositions on "The seasons in Japan".

(1) Natalie's composition
I like spring in Japan best. When spring comes, the cherry trees bloom. Cherry blossoms are very beautiful. Also, spring isn't hot, so it's nice for walks.

(2) Ali's composition
In my country it is hot all year round. So I saw snow for the first time in Japan. The snow was white and very cold. I want to see snow again next winter.

blanks.e: はなが さく: to bloom.
それに: besides, also.
ですから: that's why (he had never seen snow).
ます-stem + たい.

tg010.tt:
In class, students wrote compositions on "My day".

(1) Sofia's composition
I get up at 6 every morning. After getting up, I take a shower. Then I eat breakfast and go to school. School is from 9 to 3.

(2) Carlos's composition
I work a part-time job at night, so I can't get up early in the morning. I always get up around 10. My classes are only in the afternoon, so it's OK. But I'd like to get up earlier.

blanks.e: 〜て から: after.
〜から 〜まで.
はやく おきる: to get up early.
でも: but (contrast with "it's OK").

tg011.tt:
International students wrote compositions on "My friend".

(1) Min's composition
My friend Tanaka is Japanese. Tanaka teaches me Japanese. I teach Tanaka Korean. Studying together is fun.

(2) Luca's composition
My friend Kate came from America. Kate is tall and has long hair. She is a very cheerful person, so everyone likes her.

blanks.e: 〜て くれる: someone does something for me.
〜て あげる: I do something for someone else.
〜から くる: to come from.
She's cheerful, so everyone likes her.

tg012.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "My room".

(1) Jack's composition
My room is small, but it's bright, because the window is big. There is a desk in front of the window. I like studying there.

(2) Lisa's composition
There are lots of books in my room. The books that don't fit on the bookshelf I put on the desk. I plan to buy a new bookshelf soon.

blanks.e: でも/が after せまい: something positive; the reason is the big window → あかるい.
dictionary form + のが すき.
The books that don't fit on the bookshelf.
dictionary form + つもり.

tg013.tt:
Students at a Japanese language school wrote compositions on "Birthdays".

(1) Park's composition
Last week was my birthday. My classmates threw a party for me. We ate cake, sang songs, and so on. It was a lot of fun.

(2) Ana's composition
My birthday is next month. My mother back home always sends me a present. This year I'm in Japan, so I can't see my mother. I'm a little lonely.

blanks.e: They did something for me: 〜て くれました.
A past party: past tense.
My mother sends to me: 〜て くれます.
dictionary form + ことが できる.

tg014.tt:
International students wrote compositions on "Life in Japan".

(1) Mark's composition
It has been three months since I came to Japan. At first I didn't understand Japanese at all, and it was hard. Now I understand a little.

(2) Chen's composition
I like Japanese trains. From the train window you can see all kinds of towns. But the trains are always crowded, and I can't sit down. Mornings are hard.

blanks.e: Cause: わからなくて たいへんでした.
でも: contrast (he likes them, but they're crowded).
〜ことが できない.
In the morning, with so many people, it's tough: たいへん.

tg015.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "Food in my country".

(1) Juan's composition
In my country, we eat lunch late. We eat around 2 o'clock, and we have dinner around 10. It's quite different from Japan, isn't it?

(2) Ami's composition
Food in my country is very spicy. Japanese food isn't very spicy. So sometimes I start wanting to eat food from my country. Next week I plan to cook food from my country for my friends.

blanks.e: Eating at 2 = late: おそいです.
Tricky one: ずいぶん (quite), affirmative.
ですから: that's why she misses spicy food.
I do something for my friends: 〜て あげる.

tg016.tt:
In Japanese class, students wrote compositions on "My dream".

(1) Sam's composition
In the future I want to work at a Japanese company. For that, I'm studying Japanese very hard now.

(2) Lucy's composition
I like children, so I want to become an elementary school teacher. Now I'm studying at university. And after I graduate, I plan to go back to my country and become a teacher.

blanks.e: ます-stem + たい.
〜に なりたい.
そして: and (then).
〜つもりです: to intend to.

tg017.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "Rainy days".

(1) Oliver's composition
I don't like rainy days, because when it rains you can't play soccer outside. On rainy days I always play video games at home.

(2) Hana's composition
I like rainy days. I like reading books while listening to the sound of the rain. Also, the town is quiet on rainy days. It rained yesterday too, so I read two books at home.

blanks.e: You can't play outside, that's why he doesn't like it.
ます-stem + ながら.
それに: besides, also.
きのう → affirmative past.

tg018.tt:
International students wrote compositions on "Places I want to go in Japan".

(1) Nick's composition
I want to go to Kyoto. There are many old temples in Kyoto. I've seen them in photos, and they were very beautiful. Someday I want to go and see them with my own eyes.

(2) Yuri's composition
I want to climb Mt. Fuji. But Mt. Fuji is very high, so climbing it alone is scary. I'm thinking I'd like to climb it with friends.

blanks.e: Temples (things): ある.
いつか: someday.
Climbing such a high mountain alone is scary: こわい.
〜たいと おもって います.

tg019.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "My school".

(1) Kevin's composition
My school is a five-minute walk from the station. It's very convenient. There are about 200 students at the school. There are students from many countries.

(2) Rina's composition
The teachers at my school are all kind. When there's something I don't understand, they always explain it carefully. I love my school.

blanks.e: とても + affirmative.
ぐらい: about.
The teachers teach me: 〜て くれます.
Positive context: だいすき.

tg020.tt:
In Japanese class, students wrote compositions on "My weekend".

(1) Ivan's composition
Last Saturday I went over to a friend's house. My friend's mother made us a delicious dinner. After that, we all watched a movie together.

(2) Sora's composition
On Sunday I was at home all day. I did things like the laundry and cleaning my room. At night I was tired and went to bed early.

blanks.e: She did it for us: 〜て くれました.
それから: and then, after that.
〜たり 〜たり する.
Adverb: はやく ねる.

tg021.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "Pets".

(1) Ben's composition
We have two dogs at home. Both dogs are white and small. Every morning I walk in the park with the dogs.

(2) Mia's composition
I like cats. But in my current apartment, pets aren't allowed. So I often go to a cat café. Playing with the cats there is something I look forward to.

blanks.e: Tricky one: どちらの 〜も, both (of two).
〜ては いけません.
それで: that's why she goes to the cat café.
Positive context: たのしみ.

tg022.tt:
International students wrote compositions on "Part-time jobs".

(1) George's composition
I have a part-time job at a restaurant near the station. I work three times a week, from 6 to 10 p.m. The work is hard, but I use a lot of Japanese, so it's good study.

(2) Eri's composition
I don't have a part-time job yet. I plan to look for one after my Japanese gets a little better. I'd like to try working at a convenience store.

blanks.e: 〜から 〜まで.
Plain form before ので.
Tricky one: 〜て から, after it improves.
Tricky one (N4): 〜て みたい, to want to try.

tg023.tt:
In class, students wrote compositions on "Winter vacation".

(1) Laura's composition
During winter vacation I went back to my country. Winter in my country is much colder than in Japan. It was snowing a lot. I spent the time with my family, and it was a lot of fun.

(2) Tao's composition
I didn't go back to my country during winter vacation. So I spent New Year's in Japan. I went to a temple with friends and drew an omikuji (fortune slip).

blanks.e: より ずっと: much more. あまり/ぜんぜん/すこしも need a negative.
Cause: 〜て たのしかった.
ですから: that's why she spent New Year's in Japan.
おみくじを ひく: to draw a fortune slip.

tg024.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "My favorite season".

(1) Max's composition
I like summer, because in summer you can swim in the sea. Last summer I went to the sea every week.

(2) Aya's composition
I like autumn best. It's neither hot nor cold, so it's a nice season. Also, fruit is delicious in autumn. I like apples, so when autumn comes I eat them every day.

blanks.e: He likes it because he can swim.
〜も 〜も ありません: neither… nor…
それに: besides, also.
A habit: present tense.

tg025.tt:
Students living in Japan wrote compositions on "My country".

(1) Camila's composition
My country is Brazil. Brazil is very far from Japan. It takes about 24 hours by plane. But many Japanese people live in Brazil.

(2) Johan's composition
My country is Germany. German people like beer. There are all kinds of beer in my country. I can't drink beer, but I like sausages.

blanks.e: 24 hours by plane: far.
わたしの くに.
dictionary form + ことが できる.
でも/が after not being able to drink: something positive, he likes sausages.

tg026.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "My breakfast".

(1) Rick's composition
I eat bread every morning. In my country I also had bread. But Japanese bread is soft and very delicious.

(2) Yumi's composition
At my house, breakfast is always rice and miso soup. My mother makes it for us every morning. But on days when my mother is busy, I make it. I'm still bad at cooking, but I can make miso soup well.

blanks.e: でも: contrast.
My mother makes it for me.
On those days she makes it.
まだ へた ですが…

tg027.tt:
International students wrote compositions on "Buses in Japan".

(1) Eric's composition
On Japanese buses, you get on at the back and get off at the front. It's the opposite of my country. At first I didn't know that.

(2) Mina's composition
I go to school by bus every day. On the bus I always read Japanese books. Also, it's quiet on the bus. Yesterday the bus was late, and I was late for school.

blanks.e: Tricky one: はんたい (the opposite).
いつも + affirmative.
それに: besides, also.
The bus was late.

tg028.tt:
In class, students wrote compositions on "My favorite place".

(1) Tony's composition
I like the bookstore near the station. There's a café inside the bookstore, and you can read books while drinking coffee.

(2) Aya's composition
I like the river near my house. I walk along that river every morning. In spring the cherry trees bloom, and it's very beautiful. Next time, I'm thinking I'd like to take my friends there.

blanks.e: 〜ながら: while.
その: the river already mentioned.
さくらが さく.
〜たいと おもう.

tg029.tt:
Students wrote compositions on "When I'm sick".

(1) Ken's composition
Last week I caught a cold and got a fever. I was absent from school for three days. A friend came to my house and showed me his notes. I was very happy.

(2) Lisa's composition
When I'm sick, I always eat fruit, because fruit is good for your body. In my country, my mother used to cut apples for me.

blanks.e: ねつが でる.
He showed them to me: 〜て くれました.
Tricky one: なぜなら 〜から, because.
りんごを きって くれる.

tg030.tt:
In Japanese class, students wrote compositions on "Shopping".

(1) Mario's composition
On the weekend I went to the department store to buy shoes. There were some nice shoes, but they were expensive. So I didn't buy any.

(2) Nana's composition
I like shopping at the supermarket. If you go around 8 p.m., the bread and boxed lunches get cheaper.

blanks.e: いい くつが ありました が…
それで: so, that's why.
〜のが すき.
i-adj + く なる.
